hints.content:
We are trying to find a **unit rate**, specifically the number of cars sold per $1$ year.

$\dfrac{\blueE{\text{cars}}}{\maroonD{\text{years}}} = \purpleD{\text{cars per year}}$

We can compare from the largest to the smallest place value.

###Finding the unit rates

We divide based on the unit rate we want, not the order of the columns in the original table.

Car salesperson| $\blueE{\text{Cars sold}}$ || $\maroonD{\text{Years of}}$ $\maroonD{\text{employment}}$|| $\purpleE{\text{Cars sold}}$ $\purpleE{\text{per year}}$
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Ronaldo |$104$|$\div$ | $2$|$=$|$52$
Maria|$322$ |$\div$ |$7$ | $=$|$46$
Bruno |$516$ |$\div$ | $12$|$=$| $43$

###Comparing the unit rates

Car salesperson | Tens | Ones
- | :-: | :-:| :-:|:-:|:-:
Ronaldo | $\redE{5}$ | $2$
Maria| $4$ | $6$
Bruno | $4$ | $3$

Ronaldo sold the most tens of cars per year.

###Conclusion

Ronaldo sold the most cars per year.

question.content:
There are three car salespeople at the local car dealership. The table below shows how many cars each salesperson has sold.

Car salesperson | Years of employment | Cars sold 
- | :-: | :-:
Ronaldo|$2$ | $104$
Maria |$7$ | $322$ 
Bruno | $12$  | $516$ 

**Which car salesperson sold the most cars per year?**
